literal: Reached the highest state, completely renounced (they); having been deluded, fell into a net, other they.
translation: Those who have completely renounced have reached the highest state. The others, being deluded, are caught in a net.
modern: முற்றிலுமாகப் பற்றுக்களைத் துறந்தவர்கள் உயர்ந்த நிலையை அடைந்தவர்கள் ஆவர். அவ்வாறு துறக்காத மற்றவர்கள் மயக்கமடைந்து வலையில் அகப்பட்டவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts those who have fully renounced attachments with those who have not. The phrase 'தீரத் துறந்தார்' refers to those who have completely given up desires, and they are said to have 'தலைப்பட்டார்', meaning they have reached the highest state. The word 'தலை' (head) is used here in the sense of 'highest' or 'ultimate', which best fits the goal of renunciation. On the other hand, 'மற்றையவர்' (the others) are 'மயங்கி' (deluded by worldly illusions) and thus 'வலைப்பட்டார்', trapped in the net of worldly suffering.
